what_its_for: Nilutamide is used to treat prostate cancer in men. It works by blocking the effects of male hormones (like testosterone) that can help prostate cancer cells grow. It is usually used together with a surgical procedure called orchiectomy (removal of the testicles) to help stop the spread of prostate cancer.
how_to_take: Take nilutamide by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not crush, break, or chew the tablet.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 300 mg (three 100 mg tablets) taken once a day for the first 30 days. After that, the dose is usually lowered to 150 mg (one and a half tablets) taken once a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your situation.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next scheduled dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store nilutamide at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in a dry place away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medication properly — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking nilutamide. Alcohol can cause a serious reaction including flushing, fast heartbeat, low blood pressure, and nausea. Avoid driving at night or in low-light conditions because nilutamide can slow your eyes' ability to adjust to changes in light. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines you take, including vitamins and supplements, as nilutamide can interact with many medications including blood thinners like warfarin and certain seizure medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: shortness of breath or difficulty breathing (this could be a sign of a serious lung problem); chest pain; yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); vision changes or severe sensitivity to light; swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles; severe dizziness or fainting; unusual bleeding or bruising; signs of a serious skin reaction such as a rash, blistering, or peeling skin. Also call your doctor if your cancer symptoms seem to be getting worse.
when_it_works: Nilutamide starts working shortly after you begin taking it, but it may take several weeks to months before you or your doctor can measure how well it is controlling your prostate cancer. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own, even if you feel well. Keep all of your scheduled lab tests and doctor appointments so your doctor can check how well the medicine is working and watch for side effects.
special_populations: Liver problems: Nilutamide is NOT recommended if you have severe liver disease. Your doctor will check your liver with blood tests before you start and regularly while you are on this medicine. Lung problems: Tell your doctor if you have ever had lung disease. Nilutamide can rarely cause a serious lung condition called interstitial pneumonitis. Kidney problems: Use with caution if you have kidney problems; your doctor may need to monitor you more closely. Older adults: Older men may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine. Women and children: This medicine is only for adult men with prostate cancer. It should NOT be used by women or children. Pregnancy warning: Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should not handle or take this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby.
